title: Three-Dimensional Structural Analysis of Templated Gold Nanoplates by Integrating Electron Tomography and 4D-STEM
content: Gold nanoplates represent a promising class of nanomaterials with exceptional optical and electronic properties that make them suitable for applications in plasmonics, catalysis, and sensing. Their large aspect ratio and anisotropic morphology enable tunable surface plasmon resonances (SPRs), yet their inherent mechanical flexibility makes them susceptible to deformation [1]. The interplay between mechanical deformation and electronic structure in these nanoplates remains underexplored, requiring advanced characterization techniques to elucidate structural changes at the nanoscale level. Here, we integrate four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) and electron tomography to examine the three-dimensional structure and strain of deformed gold nanoplates on hollow silica (SiO2) spheres, adhered via van der Waals forces.
